transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-25 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Arboretum Head of Search), Ethan Cole (Arboretum Platform Eng), Rosa Jimenez (Arboretum CTO)

Auto-generated summary: quick hosted demo of embeddings + rerank endpoints, high-level cost/latency guidance, agree next steps for pilot and security review.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm Maya, i'm the account lead for redwood inference. quick round-robin?
[00:05] Priya: hey Priya here, head of search at arboretum.
[00:07] Ethan: Ethan, platform eng.
[00:08] Rosa: rosa, cto, dropping in for the security parts.
[00:11] Lucas: Lucas, solutions engineer. i'll take the demo portion and the benchmarking questions.
[00:15] Maya: great. objective today is to show the hosted API flow for embeddings plus our reranker endpoint, how you'd wire the candidate generation -> rerank path, and give some guidance on latency/cost tradeoffs for your product search workload. we'll leave time for security and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Priya: perfect. prioritized metrics for us are top-1 accuracy lift, and sub-100ms median latency on rerank if possible, but cost is obviously a concern.
[00:38] Lucas: noted. quick preface: our hosted embeddings endpoint returns a 1536-d vector (or smaller depending on model) and is optimized for fast batching. rerank endpoint accepts your original query, a list of candidate doc ids plus their embeddings or text, and produces a score and optional explanation tokens.
[00:58] Ethan: question — can the rerank call accept precomputed doc embeddings or do we need to pass raw text?
[01:04] Lucas: good question. you can pass precomputed embeddings, which is usually cheaper — we just do a light attention layer on top for contextual scoring. that helps if you already have an embedding index in something like weaviate or elastic. if you pass raw text, our pipeline will compute embeddings server-side then run the reranker, which is simpler but higher cost.
[01:22] Priya: what's the typical latency difference? ballpark numbers are fine.
[01:27] Lucas: for precomputed embeddings, median per-request rerank time is often 30–80ms for a 10-candidate batch on a hosted medium model. if you let the hosted API compute embeddings + rerank in a single request, it moves to 80–200ms depending on model and sequence length. we measure on real workload distributions though — your document lengths matter.
[01:48] Rosa: and batching? you mentioned 10 candidates — what about 50?
[01:52] Lucas: abso — at 50 candidates we see latency increase and utility of batching kicks in. we do continuous batching on the server, but per-request p99 can jump into 300–500ms range for large candidate sets on hosted tiers. that's where our recommendations in the console Optimize tab come in: it will suggest a quantization profile or to offload heavy reranks to a dedicated pool if you need consistent sub-200 p99.
[02:15] Maya: i'm going to share my screen with the studio quickstart and the console so you can see the code snippets. bear with me while i switch windows.
[02:30] [screen share begins]
[02:32] Lucas: i'll walk through an example. here's a simple pipeline we recommend: 1) client hits search service -> 2) vector store returns top-K candidates (we recommend K=50 for recall) -> 3) call redwood rerank with precomputed embeddings for efficiency -> 4) apply business rules and respond.
[02:51] [00:03:00] Priya: are there any hard limits on payload size? our search returns up to 50 items with ~2k chars each in the snippet — will that cause issues?
[03:10] Lucas: the hosted rerank endpoint has a max request size (~1.5MB on default plans); for large snippets we recommend sending embeddings only or truncate the snippet to the relevant window. passing the raw texts for 50 large docs can push you over the limit. if you need full content, we often recommend precomputing embeddings and sending those.
[03:29] Ethan: how does billing work — separate charges for embeddings and rerank?
[03:33] Maya: yes, embeddings are billed per embedding unit and rerank is billed per token equivalent + a small per-request surcharge for contextual scoring. we'll send exact pilot pricing, but in practice combining precomputed embeddings with a lightweight reranker reduces the per-query cost by ~30–60% vs doing everything server-side.
[03:52] Priya: ok. show us an example request/response?
[03:55] Lucas: sure — here's a curl sample.
[03:58] Lucas: "curl POST /v1/embeddings with body {text: [...]}" returns embeddings array; then "POST /v1/rerank" with {query: "blue shoes", candidates: [{id: 1, embedding: [...]}, ...]} returns {scores: [...], winner: id}. i'll paste both examples into the chat.
[04:20] [04:35] Priya: hmm in our stack we use an in-house faiss cluster. any gotchas integrating?
[04:40] Lucas: none major — just ensure your embedding dimensionality and normalization match. we also provide a small client library that transforms candidate sets into the rerank payload. and you can route rerank traffic to a dedicated pool if you want predictable throughput — more on that in a sec.
[04:57] Rosa: on security, we need SOC2, SSO, and the ability to hold audit logs for queries. do you support KMS?
[05:06] Maya: yes. hosted plans support envelope encryption and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. we can share SOC2 docs after the call. audit logs and token-level traces are available in the console; retention windows are configurable as a paid add-on.
[05:20] Rosa: and data residency — some EU rules apply to our EU customers. can you pin region?
[05:24] Maya: hosted is region-aware — we have EU regions and explicit routing. for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) deployment. we can discuss that during the follow-up.
[05:37] Ethan: you mentioned Optimize recommendations in the console — can it recommend quantization profiles?
[05:42] Lucas: yes. Optimize collects latency/cost metrics and suggests batch sizes, caching TTLs, and model quantization (8-bit/4-bit) given your workload. it outputs expected cost savings and a confidence band. it's a good starting point for pilots.
[06:00] Priya: what about model drift and quality monitoring? we have messy logs and want to detect regressions after deploy.
[06:06] Lucas: our evals and quality monitors let you track a prompt set and auto-surfacing score regressions. you can attach specific prompt sets to a rollout so if reranker quality drops, we alert and optionally auto-fallback to prior model versions.
[06:22] Rosa: is fallback instantaneous? like if a model is slower or overloaded.
[06:26] Lucas: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies — routing by latency SLO or cost threshold. customers commonly set a canary followed by an automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency or errors spike.
[06:40] Maya: switching to an integration snippet. here's Node/Python examples for sending precomputed embeddings to rerank. note the client side we recommend doing normalization and optional PCA if you need to reduce vector size.
[06:57] [07:10] Ethan: do you support cosine vs dot product? our vector store is tuned for cosine.
[07:14] Lucas: rerank accepts raw embeddings; we apply the similarity function you choose. for cross-compatibility, using l2-normalized vectors for cosine is typical. we'll note this in the integration doc we'll send.
[07:30] Priya: about metrics — you mentioned p50/p95 earlier — we care about p95 more. what should we expect for p95 on hosted for 10 candidates precomputed?
[07:40] Lucas: p95 is often ~120–250ms on hosted standard region; p99 can spike if there's a big inbound burst. for strict p95 targets under 200ms we recommend either reducing candidate set to ~10–20 or using dedicated capacity.
[07:54] Rosa: how fast can a dedicated capacity be provisioned?
[07:58] Maya: typical lead times depend on contract — reserved capacity can be available within 48–72 hours for standard node types. for enterprise private deployments it can be a few weeks.
[08:12] [08:20] Priya: for our pilot we'd like to test 10k queries/day at peak, mostly on product search, with median doc size ~300 tokens. will hosted suffice?
[08:29] Lucas: hosted should be fine for that volume. cost will depend on candidate count and whether you precompute embeddings. worst case, if you do server-side embeddings + rerank for 10k q/day with K=50, costs add up. recommended pilot: precompute embeddings, keep K at 20 for rerank, and use Optimize to set batching.
[08:49] Ethan: what about caching — if a query repeats often can we cache rerank results?
[08:53] Lucas: yes, prefix caching and KV cache for repeated prompts is supported — the console can estimate hit rates. for search we often cache top results for short TTLs (30s-5m) to balance freshness.
[09:06] Priya: are there any gotchas with tokenization differences between our indexer and reranker?
[09:11] Lucas: small ones — we use a consistent tokenizer per model. if you rely on substring heuristics, mismatches can occur. sending embeddings avoids tokenization mismatches.
[09:22] [09:40] Maya: quick detour — competitors — we see folks using vertex endpoints or managed openai embeddings then a homegrown rerank. the advantage of redwood here is integrated rerank that is tuned for production economics and built-in rollouts.
[09:55] Priya: ok demo time — Lucas, walk us through a live rerank call with precomputed embeddings.
[10:01] Lucas: sure. i'm going to run a sample payload from our sandbox that mimics your product catalog. note this is synthetic.
[10:08] [screen: terminal runs curl with 10 candidate embeddings]
[10:12] Lucas: response comes back in 140ms. scores are inlined and we return a short explanation token window. see the score distribution in the console trace.
[10:20] Priya: nice. can we see how this looks in the console for traces and per-request cost breakdown?
[10:25] Lucas: switching to console. here's the per-request trace: token counts, embedding time, rerank time, and cost estimate. you can click into model-level metrics and see per-route SLAs.
[10:37] Ethan: nice, that trace view will help our SREs. does the console export CSV/BigQuery?
[10:42] Lucas: yes exports to S3/BigQuery and we have a webhook for streaming traces to your observability pipeline.
[10:47] Priya: what about rerank explainability — our product team needs to see why an item was boosted.
[10:52] Lucas: the reranker can optionally return attribution tokens or log gradients-like scores for each candidate; we also provide a compact explanation in the response. keep in mind enabling detailed attribution can increase response size and cost.
[11:06] Rosa: on compliance — you said SOC2 and KMS, but can we get a data processing addendum?
[11:11] Maya: yes we have a DPA template for enterprise customers and can feed it into legal. we'll attach it to the pilot paperwork.
[11:19] [11:30] Ethan: latency during bursts — what's the rate limiting model? per-tenant qps?
[11:36] Lucas: hosted has soft rate limits per API key and token quotas. for sustained high throughput we recommend dedicated pools. soft limits help us protect noisy tenants; you can request higher limits for pilots.
[11:48] Priya: ok, curious about the data flow for precomputed embeddings: we keep embeddings in Faiss, then for rerank we fetch top-K embeddings, then call your rerank. is there any serialization/overhead we should optimize?
[12:00] Lucas: keep embeddings as binary float32 or float16 and avoid JSON payload bloat — our client libs support a compact binary gRPC path for high-throughput scenarios. for hosted HTTP flows, use base64-encoded vectors but try to batch candidates.
[12:18] Priya: base64 bloat is a real thing, yeah.
[12:21] Lucas: right — that's why many integrate via our SDK which handles compact transfers automatically.
[12:28] [12:40] Maya: let's talk pilot scope & timeline briefly. recommended pilot: 2–3 weeks, focus on a single product vertical, 5k-10k daily queries, run rerank with K=20 precomputed embeddings, compare top-1 accuracy against current baseline, gather latency and cost CSVs.
[12:56] Priya: that sounds reasonable. what are the acceptance criteria?
[12:59] Maya: increase in top-1 click-through or NDCG@10 by X% (we'll help define X with your data), p95 latency under 250ms for rerank with the specified K, and operational readiness (traces + export).
[13:12] Priya: we'll draft that and send it back.
[13:15] Lucas: i'll note that for the follow-up.
[13:18] [13:30] Ethan: security follow-up — Rosa is interested in private deployment options too; can we see a whitepaper?
[13:36] Maya: yes we'll attach Private deployment architecture and the VPC network diagram.
[13:40] Rosa: and minimum hardware requirements?
[13:42] Maya: for private clusters we provide an on-prem pack and recommended node types; again i'll share that doc.
[13:48] Priya: one last technical question — how deterministic is reranker scoring? we need reproducible scores for A/B.
[13:56] Lucas: score nondeterminism can occur with stochastic sampling models; our reranker uses a deterministic scoring head for ranking so results are reproducible given the same inputs and model version. if you enable sampling for generation-style outputs that's a different story.
[14:10] [14:30] Maya: okay we're coming up on time. quick recap and next steps.
[14:33] Lucas: recap from SE: recommend precompute embeddings in your faiss, K=20 for pilot, run bench with provided payloads, share CSVs.
[14:43] Maya: from AE: i'll send pilot pricing, soc2 + DPA, private deployment whitepaper, and a one-page integration checklist.
[14:50] Priya: i'll send internal success criteria and confirm stakeholders.
[14:53] Ethan: we'll upload sample queries by next week to the s3 link.
[14:58] Rosa: legal will review the DPA, expect questions on retention windows.
[15:02] Maya: great. final Qs?
[15:05] Priya: none for now. thanks a lot, this was helpful.
[15:08] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the noted artifacts.
[15:12] [meeting end]
